bug_semantics: CMS Asset Manager (modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php) allowed SVG uploads and wrote the file to theme assets with only extension/size/validity checks. There was no SVG sanitization on upload, so a backend user with cms.manage_assets could store an SVG containing scriptable markup. The file is then served/previewed as a theme asset (stored XSS / CWE-79). CSRF and a valid backend session are required.
flaw_origin: Unsanitized SVG-allowed asset upload was first written when modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php was added in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 (2014-05-14, Sam Georges). That commit set allowedAssetTypes including svg and checkUploadPostback() moved the uploaded file with no Svg::extract/sanitize. Parent d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 has no AssetList.php. Later c03fd66aeb8a6f10290381a76db0867fabe881e6 only renamed the postback uploader to onUpload(); that is a refactor, not the BIC.
